decision:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at EXL3 2.75 bpw across both Sparks (2026-10-19). Chosen for quality: the lowest measured KLD of any two-Spark quant (0.0201; code 0.0125), Engram tables unquantized on NVMe; 3.5 bpw builds do not fit. DeepSWE 77.0 vs 54.4 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 42.3 vs 7.0 over the 0731 model on DeepSeek's harness, and faster here: 96 vs 67 tok/s on code. The separate VLM is retired; this model serves vision. Previous decision kept below. Full reasoning in deploy/spark/README.md and NEXT_SESSION.md 2026-10-19.

PREVIOUS: DeepSeek-V4-Flash official FP8 across both DGX Sparks, vLLM tensor-parallel, B12X MoE kernel (2026-08-23). The second Spark arrived and settled the question the previous entry deferred: the official checkpoint is ~167 GB and does not fit on one box, so TP=2 is a requirement rather than a preference. Same model as before, but at release precision instead of a ~2-bit GGUF, and the thing that actually mattered was not speed - the new engine enforces JSON schemas, which the old one ignored. That removed the only reason six roles were pinned to a 4B, and 287 lines of workaround (JSONFallbackWriter, FallbackInferenceProvider) were deleted with it. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B was the better engineering fit - 25 GB, one box, 218-436 tok/s, perfect tool-calling - and was rejected on intelligence: 32 on the Artificial Analysis index against DeepSeek's 52, SWE-bench 73.4 against 79. The cost of that choice is stated plainly: both boxes are consumed, so image generation has no home on this hardware and vision keeps the ~27 GB left per box. Biggest single win was free: the boot log showed 'Using DEEPGEMM_MXFP4' - a silent fallback - and adding --moe-backend flashinfer_b12x, with no change to the model, took code decode from 26.2 to 63.5 tok/s. Full reasoning in docs/MODEL_EVALUATION.md.
